Lors de sa réunion annuelle, l'IATA (Association du transport aérien international) annonce des marges revues à la baisse pour 2026, à 2% contre 4,2 % en 2025. Le bénéfice net anticipé est de seulement 23 milliards $ pour 2026, presque moitié moins que les 45 milliards $ de 2025, ce qui représente 4,50$ par passager transporté au lieu des 9,10 $ constatés l'année dernière. La guerre au Moyen-Orient ébranle tout le secteur, entre perturbations de l'espace

france24fr.title: Mesures sécuritaires au Mali: des zones d'intérêt militaires interdites aux civils
france24fr.description: Au Mali, face aux djihadistes qui mènent de plus en plus d'attaques vers le sud du pays, la junte malienne prend des décisions. L’une des dernières en date, l’instauration des zones d’intérêts militaires sur le territoire malien.

france24fr.title: "Fawn Mianju" : cette ingérence étrangère "made in China"
france24fr.description: Viginum, l'organisme français chargé de prévenir les ingérences numériques étrangères, a identifié un vaste réseau de propagande venu de Chine. Des pseudo-sites d'actualité et des comptes sur les réseaux sociaux visant à promouvoir la Chine, en lien direct avec la chaîne de télévision d'état chinoise CGTN.

france24fr.title: Faute d'accord entre Dassault et Airbus, Berlin et Paris enterrent leur avion de combat commun
france24fr.description: La bataille d'égo entre Dassault et Airbus a conduit à la fin du projet d'un avion de combat européen. Emmanuel Macron et son homologue allemand Friedrich Merz ont regretté "l'impossibilité pour les industriels de s'entendre sur la continuation de ce projet" initié en 2017 qui devait permettre à l'Europe de se doter d'avions de combat de sixième génération.

france24fr.title: "Darmanin démission", "Justice pour nos filles" : des manifestants en colère après l'affaire Lyhanna
france24fr.description: Des rassemblements ont eu lieu en début de soirée lundi devant les tribunaux de plus de 160 villes pour dénoncer le traitement policier et judiciaire des violences sexuelles en France, après la mort de la jeune Lyhanna, victime d'un pédocriminel.

france24fr.title: Iran-Israël : l'escalade malgré Trump ?
france24fr.description: Israël et l'Iran ont lancé lundi des attaques réciproques après les tirs de missiles iraniens en direction du territoire israélien, menaçant la trêve en vigueur et les espoirs de Donald Trump d'arriver à un accord pour mettre fin à la guerre au Moyen-Orient. Téhéran a annoncé à la mi-journée une "cessation" des frappes contre Israël, alors que le Sud-Liban reste sous le feu israélien.

france24fr.title: Journée mondiale des océans: un pilier du climat à protéger
france24fr.description: En cette journée mondiale des Océans, 29 chercheurs de 14 pays ont publié la 2è édition du baromètre Starfish sur la santé des fonds marins. Un outil créé l'an dernier à la conférence de Nice. Les scientifiques notent une dégradation des différents indices et dénoncent des pressions humaines accrues sur les océans. Ils s'inquiètent aussi de la politique de l'administration américaine qui supprime des outils de surveillance des océans tant dans l'Atlantique que dans le Pacifique.

france24fr.title: Zverev à Roland-Garros : le sacre qui met les médias face à leurs contradictions
france24fr.description: Peut-on célébrer un athlète sans passer sous silence les accusations de violences conjugales qui le visent ? Après la victoire d'Alexander Zverev à Roland-Garros dimanche, les médias français ont choisi de rappeler ce contexte judiciaire. Un traitement qui témoigne d'une évolution du regard porté sur les violences sexistes et sexuelles dans le sport, même si les réflexes d'euphémisation demeurent.

france24fr.title: Mort de Lyhanna : un scandale d'État ?
france24fr.description: "Quand on a un schéma de répétition de faits divers, on est dans un phénomène de société", alerte Laurent Boyet, président et fondateur de l'association "Les Papillons". Ce lundi, des rassemblements sont prévus dans toute la France après le meurtre de Lyhanna, 11 ans, dans le Gers. Les ministres de la justice et de l'intérieur Gérald Darmanin et Laurent Nuñez sont auditionnés pour s'expliquer sur les failles identifiées dans cette affaire.

france24fr.title: Philippines : au moins 15 morts dans un sésime de magnitude 7,8
france24fr.description: Un séisme de magnitude 7,8 a frappé les Philippines, provoquant des secousses violentes ressenties dans plusieurs régions du pays et déclenchant des alertes aux risques de dégâts importants et de possibles répliques. Les autorités parlent d'au moins 15 morts et des dizaines de blessés.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le meilleur arbitre africain 2025 refusé sur le territoire américain
france24fr.description: L'arbitre somalien Omar Abdulkadir Artan, qui devait officier durant la Coupe du monde de football, a été refoulé à son arrivée aux États-Unis, a dénoncé lundi auprès de l'AFP un responsable somalien.

france24fr.title: En Corée du Nord, Xi Jinping promet son "soutien indéfectible" à Kim Jong-un
france24fr.description: En visite de deux jours en Corée du Nord, le président chinois Xi Jinping a dit lundi apporter "son soutien indéfectible" au leader nord-coréen Kim Jong-un, avec qui il éprouve un "sentiment particulier de proximité". Les deux pays se sont engagés à renforcer leurs liens stratégiques et économiques.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : l’incroyable bus scolaire choisi par l’équipe de Curaçao
france24fr.description:
Pour son ultime match avant de s’envoler aux États-Unis, le plus petit pays de la compétition s’est déplacé dans un ancien bus scolaire américain.
 
La nation caribéenne abordera le tournoi dans un groupe E relevé comprenant l’Allemagne, la Côte d’Ivoire et l’Équateur pour la première Coupe du monde de son histoire.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : quelle stratégie de Sonko vis-à-vis de Diomaye Faye ?
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, Ousmane Sonko a été réélu samedi à la tête du Pastef lors du premier congrès du parti. Cette réélection intervient dans un contexte de rupture avec le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye, qui l’a limogé de la Primature en mai dernier après plusieurs mois de tensions. Fait notable, ni le chef de l’État ni les membres du Pastef restés au gouvernement n’ont été sanctionnés ou exclus du parti. Une stratégie qui interroge alors que le Sénégal traverse une importante recomposition politique. A

france24fr.title: Affaire Lyhanna : "dysfonctionnements" ou manque de moyens de la justice en France ?
france24fr.description: Depuis la découverte du corps de Lyhanna et les révélations sur les plaintes restées lettres mortes visant le principal suspect, le ministre de la Justice Gérald Darmanin a évoqué des "dysfonctionnements" et le non-respect des circulaires pour expliquer le drame. Associations et syndicats de magistrats y voient une manière pour le garde des Sceaux d'évacuer la question récurrente des moyens alloués à la justice.

france24fr.title: En Ukraine, des drones dopés à l'IA
france24fr.description: La cellule des Observateurs de France 24 a analysé des vidéos de l'armée ukrainienne qui montrent des drones en action. Certains modèles utiliseraient l'intelligence artificielle pour se déplacer et repérer sa cible, ce qui pose des questions d'utilisation de l'IA en temps de guerre mais aussi du développement de ces IA. De quoi, pourquoi pas, rebattre les cartes du conflit, comme l'explique le journaliste des Obs Guillaume Maurice.

france24fr.title: RD Congo: Hadja Labib commissaire de l'UE à la coopération internationale en visite à Bunia
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, direction Bunia en Ituri… La province reste l’épicentre de l’épidémie d’Ebola. 86 personnes y sont décédées… 488 cas confirmés y ont été recensé. Ces chiffres sont provisoires car tout le monde ne peut pas encore être testé, les autorités congolaises ne communiquent plus les cas suspects. C’est dans ce contexte que la commissaire de l’Union européenne, Hadja Labib a effectué une visite de terrain.

zeit.title: Fifa-Präsidentschaft: Platini zeigt Fifa-Chef Infantino wegen mutmaßlicher Verschwörung an
zeit.description: Michel Platini ist überzeugt, dass es bei der Fifa-Präsidentschaftswahl 2015 eine Verschwörung gegen ihn gab. Daher reichte er in Frankreich eine Strafanzeige ein.

zeit.title: USA und China: USA setzen Alibaba, BYD und Baidu auf Liste chinesischer Militärfirmen
zeit.description: Das US-Verteidigungsministerium hat weitere Unternehmen als Unterstützter von Chinas Militärs eingestuft. Dadurch kann das Pentagon keine Verträge mit ihnen abschließen.

zeit.title: Reformpläne: Beitragssatzgesetz - DRK-Präsident warnt vor Folgen
Sexueller Missbrauch: Papst Leo will die Kirche zu einem »sicheren Ort« machen
zeit.description: Bei seiner Spanienreise hat sich Papst Leo XIV. mit Missbrauchsopfern getroffen und offenbar Zugeständnisse gemacht. Wichtige Opferverbände waren nicht eingeladen.

zeit.title: iPhone-Konzern: Apple macht neuen Anlauf bei Künstlicher Intelligenz

Polizeieinsatz: Haus in Schopfheim evakuiert - Gegenstand war ungefährlich
Deutscher Sachbuchpreis: So crazy war die Deutschland-AG
zeit.description: Und wieder siegt die Historie: Konstantin Richter erhält verdient den Sachbuchpreis für seine fulminante Wirtschaftsgeschichte Deutschlands »Dreihundert Männer«.

zeit.title: Christian Eriksen: Fußballer Christian Eriksen ist zurück bei seiner Familie
zeit.description: Christian Eriksen bedankt sich nach seinem Zusammenbruch bei den Ersthelfern. Dank ihnen habe sein Defibrillator »genau das getan, wofür er entwicklt wurde«.

zeit.title: Literatur: Konstantin Richter schreibt Sachbuch des Jahres
Beste WM-Spiele: Halbfinale 2014: Bewunderung für die deutsche Demut
zeit.description: Wer das deutsche 7:1 im Halbfinale 2014 gegen Brasilien gesehen hat, wird es nie vergessen. Auch, weil die deutsche Elf nach dem Spiel viel richtig gemacht hat.

zeit.title: Ironman in Hamburg: Dann stand da plötzlich ein Sportler am Straßenrand. Und noch einer
zeit.description: Beim Hamburger Ironman schütteten Menschen Metallsplitter auf die Strecke. Sportler mussten abbrechen, verloren Zeit. Für Sascha Vetter ging es um den Traum von Hawaii.

zeit.title: Fußball: Cheerleader-Jubel zum Empfang des DFB-Teams in Winston-Salem

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Trump warnt Netanyahu vor neuem Krieg mit Iran +++ Netanyahu bestätigt Feuerpause nach Angriffen auf Iran
nzz.description: Seit April gilt eine Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und Iran. Doch am Montag griffen sich die beiden Staaten wieder gegenseitig an. Die Folgen des Konflikts sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Waffenruhe im Gazastreifen: Italien ermittelt gegen Israels rechtsextremen Polizeiminister Itamar Ben-Gvir
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Trumps zweite Amtszeit: Bundesrichter erklärt Trumps 100 000-Dollar-Visa-Gebühr für hochqualifizierte Arbeitskräfte für unzulässig
nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Noch keine Einigung über die Finanzierung der 13. AHV-Rente

nzz.description: Die deutsche Regierung zog am Montag die Reissleine, nachdem sich die beteiligten Rüstungsunternehmen nicht auf die Aufteilung der jeweiligen Anteile hatten einigen können. Für Europas Rüstung ist das ein Schlag, aber keine Katastrophe. Es gibt längst Alternativen.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Aussenminister Wadephul hat nichts aus der Niederlage in New York gelernt
nzz.description: Deutschland insistiert auf einem Sitz im Uno-Sicherheitsrat. Das zeigt ein tieferes Problem: Berlin hält seinen Machtanspruch weiterhin für selbstverständlich. Viele andere Staaten tun das längst nicht mehr.

nzz.title: Tech-Zweifel und der Krieg in Iran drücken auf die Börsenstimmung

nzz.title: Nach gegenseitigem Beschuss verkünden Israel und Iran, dass sie ihre Angriffe vorerst einstellen
nzz.description: Nach einem israelischen Angriff auf die libanesische Hauptstadt Beirut feuerte Teheran ballistische Raketen auf Israel ab. Der jüdische Staat antwortete mit Bombardierungen in Iran. Nach einem Machtwort von Donald Trump verkünden beide Seiten eine Feuerpause – doch von einer stabilen Waffenruhe kann keine Rede sein.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Tote und Verletzte nach russischen Angriffen
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: Der Bund schreibt den Schulen drei Lektionen Sportunterricht pro Woche vor. Damit könnte bald Schluss sein
nzz.description: Vertreter von Bund und Kantonen fordern das Ende der nationalen Schulsportpflicht.

nzz.title: «Die wollen Transjugendliche vernichten!» – «Die SVP hat alle Menschen gern!»
nzz.description: Im Zürcher Kantonsrat gab es am Montag kein Halten mehr. Eine Vorlage zur Gleichstellung von queeren Menschen verführte links und rechts zu abstrusen Argumenten.

nzz.title: «Gibt es weitere Fälle wie Lyhanna?» – Der Mord an einem elfjährigen Mädchen in Frankreich wird zur Justizaffäre
nzz.description: In Südfrankreich wurde vergangene Woche die Leiche der elfjährigen Lyhanna gefunden. Gegen ihren mutmasslichen Mörder lagen bereits mehrere Strafanzeigen wegen Vergewaltigungen vor. Nun lässt die Regierung rund 70 000 Fälle überprüfen, die Straftaten gegen Minderjährige betreffen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Irans Regime interessiert sich nicht für Libanon – mit seinen Raketen auf Israel testet es Trump
nzz.description: Das Regime versucht, angebliche Differenzen zwischen Trump und Netanyahu auszunutzen und damit Konzessionen am Verhandlungstisch zu erzwingen. Washington sollte hart bleiben.

nzz.title: Der Papst im spanischen Parlament: Ein Appell an Gemeinsamkeit und Humanismus
nzz.description: Leo XIV. hält in Madrid eine historische Rede und wird allseits stürmisch gefeiert. Dabei hatte er nicht nur Komplimente mitgebracht – wie vor allem die Rechtspopulisten erfahren mussten.

nzz.title: Doch keine Millionen für Choupette: Lagerfelds berühmte Katze erhält nichts aus dem Nachlass
nzz.description: Die Katze Choupette war die grosse Liebe des Modeschöpfers Karl Lagerfeld.  Nach seinem Tod hielt sich jahrelang die Legende, das berühmte Haustier werde zur Millionenerbin. Nun hat ein Gericht entschieden: Choupette geht leer aus.

nzz.title: Xi Jinping hofiert Kim Jong Un
nzz.description: Der geopolitische Spielraum von Nordkoreas Machthaber Kim Jong Un wächst weiter. Dies zeigt der erste Besuch von Chinas Staatschef in Nordkorea seit sieben Jahren.

observador.title: "UE irá defender-se de desequilíbrios" no comércio global
observador.description: "O trabalho começa em casa, reduzindo os custos energéticos e facilitando a vida às empresas em toda a Europa, mas não termina aí", disse a chefe do executivo europeu numa mensagem nas redes sociais.

observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: A catedral onde a mão de Maradona se juntou à cabeça de Pelé
observador.description: É o único recinto com duas finais de Mundiais mas também já teve Jogos Olímpicos, combates de boxe para 130.000 e velórios. Mais do que um estádio, o Azteca é história – e até o Jogo do Século foi lá.

observador.title: Greve dos registos e notariado com adesão de 52%
observador.description: Em termos de serviços encerrados, as estimativas do Instituto dos Registos e Notariado apontam para 51,2% no Continente, 100% nos Açores e 66,6% na Madeira. A greve decorre até dia 13 de junho.

observador.title: A rampa de lançamento para as startups portuguesas
observador.description: O Global Tech Innovator ajuda startups portuguesas a acelerar o crescimento, captar investimento e conquistar visibilidade. Falamos do projeto com Vasco Mendes, Partner de M&A da KPMG Portugal.

observador.title: Navegante disponibiliza informação em tempo real
observador.description: Através da plataforma, pretende-se disponibilizar dados mais fiáveis sobre horários dos transportes, sobre a localização dos veículos e sobre o estado do serviço, tornando as viagens mais previsíveis.

observador.title: Vereador do PCP questiona obras do quiosque da Estrela
observador.description: João Ferreira considera que "persistem dúvidas sobre a natureza da intervenção" e "sobre quem foi a entidade promotora da obra".

observador.title: O trunfo e o ás. Como o Benfica se enredou no poker de Pérez
observador.description: Rui Costa prometeu falar há quase um mês, mas ainda não falou. Pelo meio, esperou pelo Real – por tudo o que veio do Real. Agora, Mourinho tem um futuro no Bernabéu e Marco Silva é o futuro na Luz.

observador.title: Tubarão-branco filmado pela primeira vez no Mar Mediterrâneo
observador.description: Animal foi avistado entre a Sicília e a Tunísia, durante operação de remoção de redes de pesca abandonadas. Mergulhador que captou imagens espera que estas não causem pânico, nem captura do tubarão.

observador.title: Platini processa Infantino por denúncia caluniosa
observador.description: Além de Infantino, Platini informou também que processou Marco Villiger, antigo diretor jurídico da FIFA, e Domenico Scala, antigo responsável máximo da comissão de auditoria.

observador.title: São Jorge. Bombeiros sem capacidade para emergência noturna
observador.description: Na Comissão de Política Geral do parlamento dos Açores, Leocádia Silva recordou que este serviço, que encerrou em janeiro, foi uma opção da associação em 1996, mas "nunca constituiu uma obrigação".

observador.title: Estará Netanyahu a esticar a corda?
observador.description: Orlando Samões, especialista em Relações Internacionais, explica que pode haver uma coordenação entre EUA e Israel, apesar da violação do cessar-fogo. E ainda, analisa as eleições na Arménia.

observador.title: PSU. Bloco de Esquerda acusa Governo de seguir Chega
observador.description: Para José Manuel Pureza, coordenador nacional do BE, a proposta de Prestação Social Única tem elementos retirados da agenda do Chega, como o sistema de hipervigilância sobre titulares de prestações.

observador.title: Socialistas pedem suspensão de eleições em Coimbra
observador.description: Os militantes destacaram afirmações sigilosas de camaradas que assumem que alguém lhes pagou quotas, em determinadas secções e concelhias, e que receberam telefonemas a indicar onde votar.

observador.title: 21h. Presidente da República visita jogadores da seleção
observador.description: António José Seguro foi à cidade do futebol para dar algumas palavras de força aos jogadores. Ainda, a Iniciativa Liberal diz que o Governo está a pedir um cheque em branco na proposta da PSU.

observador.title: Guterres pede contenção para não reacender a guerra
observador.description: António Guterres instou todas as partes a respeitarem o acordo de cessar-fogo entre o Líbano e Israel, anunciado na semana passada, e a absterem-se de tomar medidas que prejudiquem a paz.

observador.title: Rendas acessíveis: AIL acusa governo de falhar fiscalização
observador.description: Criado em 2019, o PAA dá uma isenção total de impostos aos proprietários que pratiquem rendas 20% abaixo da mediana do mercado.

observador.title: Booker diz que livro de Atwood foi proibido na ditadura
observador.description: Um post nas redes sociais do prémio de ficção em língua inglesa refere que o romance de Margaret Atwood foi proibido em Portugal durante a ditadura salazarista, quando nem tinha sido publicado.

spiegel.title: Omar Artan: WM-Schiedsrichter wird Einreise in die USA verweigert

spiegel.title: Rätsel der Woche: Welcher Bruch erfüllt die Gleichung?

spiegel.title: Sohn von Mette-Marit: Marius Borg Høiby könnte vorerst freikommen

arxiv-ai.description:

Abstract: Sudoku is a representative constraint satisfaction problem that requires global structural reasoning under strict discrete constraints. The existing works of solving Sudoku mainly focus on two dominant approaches, i.e., traditional heuristic and deep learning solver. However, they suffer from two complementary limitations: learning-based solvers lack hard correctness guarantees, while complete symbolic solvers are still prone to long-tail search.

Prediction and game-theoretic planners can suggest plausible cooperation, yet they do not return a proof that the repair respects hard rules, right-of-way, cost allocation, and ego fallback. We introduce CARVE, Certified Affordable Repair of Vetoed maneuvers

Models are not static objects: they are snapshots of time-evolving processes shaped by data, objectives, architectures, and optimization dynamics. phys-org.title: Elusive Cozumel dwarf fox reappears in first confirmed photos after two decades
phys-org.description: A publication has revealed the first photographic evidence and confirmed sighting of the Cozumel dwarf fox in more than 20 years. Published in the journal Neotropical Biology and Conservation by researchers Travis D. Bayer, Maggie A. McGreal and A. Rafael Chacón D., the short communication details the rescue of an adult male Cozumel dwarf fox on the morning of Sept. 14, 2023.

phys-org.title: What happens to a star that captures a primordial black hole?
phys-org.description: We don't know whether theorized primordial black holes (PBH) are real. If they are, they formed in the very early universe, when physics was much different. They had no stellar progenitors and were created by the direct collapse of densely packed subatomic matter. Theorists have wondered whether PBH could be dark matter, or a component of dark matter.

phys-org.title: New cryogenic silicon carbide hardware addresses quantum computing bottleneck
phys-org.description: Researchers from the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering in the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Hong Kong (HKU) and the Centre for Advanced Semiconductors and Integrated Circuits (CASIC) have achieved a major breakthrough in cryogenic electronics. The team has developed a programmable neuromorphic hardware platform that operates near absolute zero, providing a potential solution for scaling up quantum computers and enabling deep-space exploration. The discovery was publ

phys-org.title: Toward standardized microplastics monitoring in rivers
phys-org.description: Microplastics (MPs), defined as plastic fragments smaller than 5 mm, have become so pervasive that they are detectable in nearly every environment studied—from remote ocean trenches to urban air, tap water, and human blood. MPs are hardly uniform; they span an enormous size range. Larger fragments are visible to the naked eye, while the smallest ones have a diameter of a few micrometers. These variations in size are important, as smaller particles are far more numerous, behave differently in wat

phys-org.title: How wax moth larvae can help reduce animal testing in research
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Helmholtz Institute for One Health (HIOH) have demonstrated that larvae of the greater wax moth, Galleria mellonella, are suitable as an alternative infection model for investigating the pathogenicity of bacteria on a larger scale. This could significantly reduce testing on mammals in the future. The results of the study were published in The Lancet Microbe.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Expert discusses 250 years of sports in the United States
phys-org.description: Sports in the United States look very different than they did when the nation was founded 250 years ago, according to Mark Dyreson, professor of kinesiology and history at Penn State. But one thing has remained constant—sport has played a vital role in shaping and reflecting the country's culture and values, he said.

phys-org.title: Medicinal plants yield carbon nanoparticles that glow red and flag toxic metals
phys-org.description: What do iron, lead and nickel have in common? These heavy metals are an indispensable part of many industries. However, they also share a dark reality: They are serious environmental and public health threats. Every day, they find their way into the atmosphere and water bodies through industrial activities, mining and urban waste. Heavy metals are highly toxic, do not break down naturally and tend to build up in the tissues of living organisms over time.

phys-org.title: 'Labubu economics': Game-theoretic model explains why blind box strategies benefit suppliers, retailers, and consumers
phys-org.description: The billion-dollar Labubu phenomenon broke a cardinal rule of retail: Consumers need to know what they're buying before they open their wallet. Most new Labubu sales took the form of "blind boxes," where purchasers found out which type of doll they'd purchased only after the fact.

phys-org.title: Ancient hominins selected basalt sources for specific tools nearly 800,000 years ago, study reveals
phys-org.description: A new study finds that ancient hominins nearly 800,000 years ago deliberately selected specific basalt sources for different stages of tool production rather than simply using whatever stone was available nearby. By tracing the geochemical "fingerprints" of stone tools to both exposed and now-buried basalt flows, the researchers demonstrated that these hominins possessed detailed environmental knowledge, advanced planning abilities, and long-term technological traditions that were maintained and

phys-org.title: New Relative Niño index introduces more robust way to measure El Niño strength
phys-org.description: A new El Niño index that provides a more climate-robust measure of the strength of El Niño signals has been released by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). With the World Meteorological Organization's recent update indicating an 80% likelihood of an El Niño event during June–August 2026 and a 90% probability of this continuing until at least November, it is more important than ever to have accurate, reliable data.

phys-org.title: Child drownings spike during heat waves—and it's a serious climate justice issue
phys-org.description: At least 15 people drowned in open water in the UK's recent heat wave, mostly children and teenagers. The public response is understandably urgent: warnings are issued, parents are told to talk to their children, and young people are reminded that rivers, lakes, reservoirs and canals can be dangerous.

phys-org.title: Plants could be used to grow medicines in space, study shows
phys-org.description: Astronauts on long space missions may one day use plants to produce fresh stocks of medicines on demand, thanks to new research by engineers at the University of California San Diego. The team developed a simple method to grow and repeatedly harvest pharmaceuticals from plants under space-like conditions, without destroying the plants or generating large amounts of waste.

phys-org.title: DNA design unlocks nanometer-scale catalyst control for cleaner hydrogen production
phys-org.description: The fixed idea that DNA is only a molecule that stores genetic information is being challenged. KAIST researchers have developed a technology that controls the chemical environment around catalysts at the nanometer scale by designing DNA sequences—the arrangement of A, T, G and C that make up genetic information. The team has presented a new catalyst platform that can improve hydrogen production efficiency and increase the yield of desired chemical products by designing DNA much like writing a c

phys-org.title: Sesame dynamically rewires lignan metabolism during germination
phys-org.description: Sesame seeds are rich in lipid-soluble lignans such as sesamin, which are widely known as health-promoting phytochemicals. While these compounds rapidly decrease during germination and are converted into water-soluble glucosides, the molecular mechanism underlying this large-scale metabolic transition had remained unclear.

phys-org.title: Corals have a hormonal clock and it looks surprisingly like ours
phys-org.description: A three-year study has cracked open the hidden biology behind coral reproduction, revealing hormone cycles that echo those of humans and other animals, and a new way to detect reef distress before it's too late.

phys-org.title: How migration became a key to World Cup success
phys-org.description: Few would have predicted Morocco's success at the 2022 Fifa World Cup. Heading into the tournament, they were ranked 22nd in the world and had never progressed beyond the round of 16.

phys-org.title: Twisted stacking lets 2D conductor keep single-layer performance in bulk form
phys-org.description: Two-dimensional (2D) materials, which are significantly thinner than a single sheet of paper, have long drawn attention for their exceptional performance. However, they have faced a critical limitation: Their performance degrades significantly when multiple layers are stacked.

phys-org.title: Green growth claims are overstated—our study shows three reasons why
phys-org.description: A holy grail of environmental policy is an economy that delivers prosperity without requiring the ever-increasing consumption of raw materials.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.
